:::{#exr-estimation-error-bound}
#### Bounding the chance of a large estimation error

Let $\hparam$ be an estimator of $\param$ with finite
[pMSE](estimation.qmd#def-mse),
and let $\varepsilon > 0$.
Use [Markov's inequality](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/limit-theorems.html#thm-markov)
to show that
$\Prf{\abs{\hparam - \param} \ge \varepsilon} \le \pMSE{\hparam} / \varepsilon^2$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-estimation-error-bound}

Both sides of $\abs{\hparam - \param} \ge \varepsilon$ are nonnegative,
so squaring them keeps the inequality.
The random variable $\sqf{\hparam - \param}$ is nonnegative,
so Markov's inequality applies to it with $a = \varepsilon^2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Prf{\abs{\hparam - \param} \ge \varepsilon}
&= \Prf{\sqf{\hparam - \param} \ge \varepsilon^2}
&& \text{(square both nonnegative sides)}\\
&\le \frac{\E{\sqf{\hparam - \param}}}{\varepsilon^2}
&& \text{(Markov's inequality, $a = \varepsilon^2 > 0$)}\\
&= \frac{\E{\sqf{\erf{\hparam}}}}{\varepsilon^2}
&& \text{(definition of the estimation error)}\\
&= \frac{\pMSE{\hparam}}{\varepsilon^2}
&& \text{(definition of the mean squared error)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
